headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure from residential ratepayers to large energy users, such as data centers, by requiring them to pay for increased generating capacity and preventing these costs from being passed on to other customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer groups, Governor's administration, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: Virginia moves to shift more power costs from families to data centers
news_summary: State regulators in Virginia are re-evaluating how to allocate the costs of significant transmission infrastructure upgrades, with a new order potentially placing a larger share of these expenses on major power consumers like data centers. This move aims to reduce the burden on households and small businesses, with the Governor's administration supporting the shift to ensure data centers cover the full cost of their required transmission infrastructure.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that waterworks operators categorize and report monthly water sales data, including potable and reclaimed water usage by data centers with state air permits, to enhance transparency and aid in water supply planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local communities, State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting in Virginia
news_summary: New regulations, effective next January, will increase transparency regarding data center water usage in Virginia by requiring waterworks operators to categorize and report monthly sales data, including usage by data centers. This legislation, championed by State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan, aims to fill data gaps for water supply planning, especially during droughts, despite individual facility data remaining protected as trade secrets.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires localities to mandate site assessments for new high-energy-use facilities, like data centers, to examine sound profiles on nearby residential units and schools, and allows for assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near potential data center sites, environmental groups.
news_headline: Data centers defined as "high-energy-use" may need noise and energy-provider disclosure
news_summary: Under HB153/SB94, facilities requiring 100 megawatts or more are now defined as "high-energy-use" and will trigger special-exception submission requirements, likely applying to data centers. Fairfax County staff propose requiring a noise study for schools and residences within 500 feet and a statement from the energy provider on anticipated demand and source.
